title: Transformations
subtitle: Slide, Flip, Turn & Dilate Points
bounds: Coordinates and transformations (PROTOCOL 4b, grade 8). Every point is an integer pair of size 10 or less before every move and after every rigid move; slides are 1-10 per axis (1-9 when both axes move); turns are 90 degrees (CW or CCW) and 180 degrees about (0, 0); flips are over the x-axis and the y-axis; dilations are about (0, 0) by scale factor 2, 3, 4, 5 or 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, only on coordinates that divide, so every image is an integer pair of size 20 or less and every product or quotient is a times-table fact (both values 10 or less). Side lengths are 2-10 before and 2-20 after a dilation; angles are multiples of 10 from 10 to 180. Rules are written (x + a, y - b) with a, b of size 10 or less. A distractor may leave these bounds (it is a wrong answer), but a right answer and every step to it stay inside.

tiers.name: Slides
tiers.description: Slide points left, right, up and down, read a slide off two points, and write its rule.

tiers.name: Flips
tiers.description: Reflect points over the x-axis and the y-axis. A flip changes one sign.

tiers.name: Turns
tiers.description: Turn points 90 or 180 degrees about (0, 0). CW is clockwise, CCW is counterclockwise.

tiers.name: Dilations
tiers.description: Dilate from (0, 0): multiply both coordinates by the scale factor.

tiers.name: Move Sequences
tiers.description: Do two moves in order, and tell congruent from similar.

REVERSED_DIRECTION.student: Right and up add. Left and down subtract. Yours went the opposite way.
REVERSED_DIRECTION.teacher: Moves the opposite way on every axis involved (adds for left or down, subtracts for right or up).

HALF_REVERSED.student: One of your directions is backwards. Right and up add; left and down subtract.
HALF_REVERSED.teacher: Applies the correct amount on both axes but reverses the direction on one of them.

SWAPPED_AMOUNTS.student: Left or right changes x, up or down changes y. Match each amount to its axis.
SWAPPED_AMOUNTS.teacher: Swaps the two amounts between the axes (the horizontal amount goes to y and the vertical to x).

ONE_AXIS.student: A slide that goes two ways changes both x and y. Do both parts.
ONE_AXIS.teacher: Applies only one of the two parts of the slide.

WRONG_AXIS.student: Left and right change x. Up and down change y.
WRONG_AXIS.teacher: Applies a horizontal slide to y (or a vertical slide to x).

IMAGE_AS_ANSWER.student: That is where the first point went. Use the same slide on the new point.
IMAGE_AS_ANSWER.teacher: Gives the image of the example point instead of applying the slide to the asked point.

ADDED_COORDS.student: Find the slide first (end minus start), then add it to the new point.
ADDED_COORDS.teacher: Adds the example image's coordinates to the asked point instead of finding the slide.

SIZE_CHANGES.student: Slides, flips and turns keep every length the same. Nothing doubles.
SIZE_CHANGES.teacher: Thinks a rigid motion scales a length (doubles or halves it).

LENGTH_CHANGES.student: Moving a shape does not change its length. The distance moved is not added.
LENGTH_CHANGES.teacher: Adds or subtracts the distance moved from the length.

ANGLE_CHANGES.student: Slides, flips and turns keep every angle exactly the same.
ANGLE_CHANGES.teacher: Believes a rigid motion changes an angle (supplement, complement or doubled).

FLIP_SUPPLEMENT.student: A flip reverses direction but keeps the angle the same size.
FLIP_SUPPLEMENT.teacher: Replaces an angle by its supplement (180 minus the angle) after a reflection.

REFLECTION_NEGATES.student: A flip turns the picture around, but an angle's size is never negative.
REFLECTION_NEGATES.teacher: Thinks a reflection makes the angle measure negative.

WRONG_MIRROR.student: Over the x-axis only y changes sign. Over the y-axis only x does.

BOTH_SIGNS.student: A flip over one axis changes just one sign. Both signs is a 180 turn.
BOTH_SIGNS.teacher: Negates both coordinates (a half turn) for a reflection.

SWAPPED_XY.student: Swapping x and y is a flip over a slanted line, not over an axis.
SWAPPED_XY.teacher: Swaps the coordinates (reflection over y = x) instead of changing a sign.

IMAGE_AS_START.student: That is the image. Flip it back over the same axis to find the start.
IMAGE_AS_START.teacher: Gives the image itself when asked for the start point (does not undo the reflection).

TURN_FOR_FLIP.student: A 180 turn changes both signs. A flip over one axis changes only one.
TURN_FOR_FLIP.teacher: Picks a half turn for a reflection (checks one coordinate only).

SLIDE_FOR_FLIP.student: A slide moves every point the same way. A flip changes a sign.
SLIDE_FOR_FLIP.teacher: Picks a slide by the coordinate's size for a reflection.

NOT_ON_AXIS.student: Only a point ON the axis stays put. Check that the other coordinate is 0.
NOT_ON_AXIS.teacher: Picks a point that is not on the axis (it moves when reflected).

NOTHING_CHANGES.student: A flip moves every point off the axis to the other side. A sign changes.
NOTHING_CHANGES.teacher: Believes a reflection changes no coordinate's sign.

WRONG_TURN.student: CCW is against the clock hands, CW is with them. Check your direction.
WRONG_TURN.teacher: Turns the right amount in the opposite direction.

SWAP_ONLY.student: A 90 turn swaps x and y AND changes one sign. Swapping alone is a flip.
SWAP_ONLY.teacher: Swaps the coordinates without a sign change (a reflection over y = x).

REFLECTED_INSTEAD.student: Changing one sign is a flip, not a turn. A turn also swaps x and y.
REFLECTED_INSTEAD.teacher: Negates one coordinate (a reflection) when a rotation was asked.

HALF_FOR_QUARTER.student: 180 changes both signs. A 90 turn swaps x and y too.
HALF_FOR_QUARTER.teacher: Uses a half turn for a quarter turn.

QUARTER_FOR_HALF.student: A 180 turn keeps x and y where they are and changes both signs.
QUARTER_FOR_HALF.teacher: Uses a quarter turn for a half turn.

ADDED_FACTOR.student: Scale factor multiplies. Multiply each coordinate by it.
ADDED_FACTOR.teacher: Adds the scale factor instead of multiplying by it.

ONE_COORD.student: A dilation scales both x and y, not just one.

INVERTED_FACTOR.student: A factor below 1 shrinks (divide by the bottom). Above 1 it grows.
INVERTED_FACTOR.teacher: Uses the reciprocal of the scale factor (enlarges for a shrink, or the reverse).

SUBTRACTED_DENOM.student: Scale factor 1/2 means half, not take away 2.
SUBTRACTED_DENOM.teacher: Subtracts the denominator instead of dividing by it.

DIFFERENCE.student: Scale factor is new over old (a ratio), not new minus old.
DIFFERENCE.teacher: Subtracts the lengths or coordinates to get the scale factor.

IMAGE_AS_FACTOR.student: The scale factor is new divided by old, not the new number itself.
IMAGE_AS_FACTOR.teacher: Gives the new length or coordinate as the scale factor.

SAME_SIZE.student: A dilation changes size. Slides, flips and turns do not.
SAME_SIZE.teacher: Believes a dilation keeps the size (treats it as rigid).

AREA_FACTOR.student: Lengths grow by the factor itself. The factor squared is for area.
AREA_FACTOR.teacher: Multiplies the length by the square of the scale factor.

ANGLES_SCALE.student: A dilation scales lengths, never angles. An angle stays the same.
ANGLES_SCALE.teacher: Multiplies or divides an angle by the scale factor.

CENTER_MOVES.student: The center of a dilation stays put. (0, 0) times anything is (0, 0).
CENTER_MOVES.teacher: Moves the center of dilation (adds the factor to the origin).

GROW_SHRINK_SWAP.student: Factor above 1 grows the figure. Factor below 1 shrinks it.
GROW_SHRINK_SWAP.teacher: Mixes up which scale factors enlarge and which shrink.

ORDER_SWAP.student: Do the moves in the order given. Slide then flip is not flip then slide.
ORDER_SWAP.teacher: Applies the two moves in the reverse order.

ONLY_FIRST.student: There is a second move. Do both, in order.

ONLY_SECOND.student: The first move changes the point too. Do both, in order.
ONLY_SECOND.teacher: Applies only the second move to the starting point.

RIGID_CHANGES_SIZE.student: Slides, flips and turns keep size. Only a dilation changes it.
RIGID_CHANGES_SIZE.teacher: Thinks a slide, flip or turn can change a shape's size.

DILATION_CONGRUENT.student: Congruent means the same size. A dilation changes size, so not congruent.
DILATION_CONGRUENT.teacher: Calls the image of a dilation congruent.

NEEDS_SAME_SIZE.student: Similar means the same shape at any size. A dilation keeps the shape.
NEEDS_SAME_SIZE.teacher: Thinks similar figures must also be the same size, so answers Neither.

COMPOSE_WRONG.student: Multiply the two scale factors to see the overall change in size.
COMPOSE_WRONG.teacher: Judges two dilations in a row without multiplying their factors.
